From: Elaine Park <elaine@thaliahealth.com>

Subject: Thalia launch — expected traffic profile and quota ask

Rafael,

Thanks again for the run-through earlier. We have a firm launch date of 2026-12-05 for our patient triage pilot and need to confirm temporary quota and burst commitments. Early projections from our infra team:

- Peak concurrent inference requests: ~30 requests/sec; expected short bursts to 60 rps for 5–10 minutes during morning triage windows.
- Estimated token volume: ~45–55M tokens/day on peak days.
- Typical request payloads: 200–600 tokens in prompts, 150–300 tokens generated (we can cap).

Two asks:
1) Temporary rate/quota increase for the week of launch (2026-12-04 to 2026-12-11) to support 60rps burst and sustained ~30rps.
2) Guidance on recommended model variant and guidance on batching/cache settings to keep latency <350ms p50.

Attaching our traffic projection worksheet. Happy to hop on a quick ops sync if helpful.

Thanks,
Elaine Park
Head of Platform, Thalia Health

Folks — forwarding Thalia's projection. They want a short-term uplift for launch week and product guidance on model variant + latency trade-offs. Quick context:

- Launch date: 2026-12-05, pilot window through 12/11.
- They expect sustained ~30rps with 60rps bursts (5–10 minute windows).
- Target latency: p50 <350ms; p95 target TBD but they'd prefer <800ms.

Questions for product/infra:
- Can we support a temporary dedicated pool (or soft quota bump) that guarantees the burst? If dedicated, what capacity estimate (GPUs / worker count)?
- Model recommendation: pick a quantized/fast variant vs. full-precision with more capacity? What are the perf/econ trade-offs?
- Any routing/cache knobs we should propose (prefix caching, batching guidance, KV cache warmup)?

Monica/Karthik — can you propose an ops playbook (pre-warm steps, gating, rollback) and a tentative quota uplift number we can commit to in a DocuSign/HubSpot request? Elaine — I'll share an ops plan + DocuSign link once we have internal alignment.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Thalia launch — expected traffic profile and quota ask

Rafael / team — sketched an operational plan and capacity ask below. High level recommendation: a short-lived dedicated pool + conservative rate caps with clear fallbacks.

Proposed capacity (sustained + burst):
- Reserve: equivalent of 2x A100-80GB GPUs (or 4x A40) for the 7-day window. This should comfortably cover sustained 30rps at a fast-medium model variant.
- Burst allowance: autoscale policy to allow 1.5x worker count for 10-minute bursts (approx to handle ~60rps); set a hard safety throttle at ~75rps.

Model variant guidance:
- Recommend using the quantized 4-bit variant we validated (Q4_0-fast) for lower latency and better throughput. Trade-off: ~1–2% quality delta for some LLM instruction tasks — acceptable for triage use-case.

Pre-warm + ops checklist:
- Warm KV prefix cache with representative prompts (we can script this).
- Apply client-side batching (prefer 2–4 requests per batch) and a max_tokens cap of 250 for responses.
- Monitor token-level cost in Console + set alert at 60% of provisioned capacity.
- Fallback policy: if latency >1s for p50, route to smaller quantized model or return a 429 with retry-after (configurable).

I'll upload a short runbook and the temporary quota request form to Drive. Attaching the filled form draft.

Monica Patel
Technical Customer Success
Redwood Inference
Attachments: temp_quota_request_form.pdf (pdf)

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thalia launch — operational checklist & gating

Thanks Monica — this looks good. A few operational notes from infra side:

- Scheduling: we can create a short-term Dedicated allocation in us-west-2. ETA to provision: ~24 hours once form + signed approval is received.
- Autoscale config: set scaling cooldown to 2 minutes and a conservative CPU/GPU utilization threshold of 65% to avoid oscillation.
- Rollback plan: if we see sustained errors above 2% for more than 10 minutes, automatic fallback to the quantized smaller model and notify CS + Account.
- Rate limiting: recommend we gate by token budget per-minute and also global rps to prevent noisy neighbors. We'll include a temporary per-api-key burst window.

Action items:
1) Rafael — get signed DocuSign for the temporary capacity request so we can provision by 2026-12-03.
2) Monica — prepare the cache-warm script and run in staging three days before launch.
3) Vivek — agree on SLA exception (p95 target and credits) for the week.

Karthik

Redwood Inference
